comment:
I don’t normally leave negative reviews in fact, I usually go out of my way to leave positive ones when I receive great service. Unfortunately, this experience was so disappointing that I felt it needed to be shared.

We visited Hector’s Deli in Richmond and ordered a cinnamon bun and an apple turnover. We politely asked if we could have a plate to make them easier to eat. Jackson simply replied, “No plate.” We said that was completely fine and then asked if we could have a box instead. We could see the pastries had already been placed into a paper bag, but instead of responding politely, he angrily shoved a box towards us. It would have taken very little effort to place the pastries into the box when we asked.

What upset me most was his attitude. When we made a simple, polite request, he gave us a dirty stare that made us feel incredibly unwelcome. We weren’t being demanding, we were just asking a reasonable question.

The interaction left such an impression that I asked another staff member for his name afterwards because I couldn’t believe how we had been treated. That’s something I’ve never felt the need to do before.

I understand that hospitality can be busy and stressful, but customers deserve to be treated with basic courtesy and respect. I genuinely hope this feedback is taken constructively, because service like this reflects poorly on an otherwise well-known business.

comment:
We came here for a late lunch and it was absolutely exquisite.
We ordered one fried chicken thigh burger with a small potato salad and matcha latte AND a spicy fried chicken breast burger with a fries.

Fried chicken thigh burger - (bun, lettuce, sauce, chicken thigh)

The chicken thigh piece they put on my burger was absolutely huge with bits poking out the side. It was 3x the scale of the bun, so I folded it onto the burger and had layers of chicken. The sauce was tangy and delicious with a strong, almost sour taste, without being overpowering at all. It blended well with the softly sweet burger bun that melted in your mouth and was perfect to accompany the chicken thigh, which was juicy, crispy and delicious. I believe the price was worth it and compared to other burger places I’ve visited, it was quite cheap ($17) for the amount of meat i got.

The potato salad was refreshing and salty with the same sourness/tangy flavour from the sauce. I was informed by the workers that they topped it with kimchi salt. I had never had that before now and I am 100% having it again. It was SO GOOD.

The matcha latte was quite ordinary, just what you would expect from a matcha latte. Earthy, smooth, slight sweetness and creamy (I had it with oat milk)

Spicy fried chicken breast burger - (bun, lettuce, chicken breast, spicy sauce)

The fried chicken fillet was cooked well - juicy, flavourful and with a crispy outside shell. Some of the best chicken I’ve had in a sandwich.
The sauce was sweet, with a mild yet flavourful spice level, which paired well with the chicken. You do get a LOT of sauce in this though, so those who like spicy sauce will love this, as did I.
The bun was soft, fluffy and buttery, offering nice support for the sauce to soak in and hold the chicken.

The fries were cooked well and seasoned in a sweet powder with salt, which may be overpowering for some but I enjoyed it very much nonetheless.

A great sandwich spot and anybody travelling in the Carlton area of Melbourne should check this place out if they haven’t already!

So many businesses talk about customer service. Hector’s actually lives it. You can tell there’s a culture of listening, accountability and genuinely caring about the people who walk through the door.

Thank you for ending my birthday week on such a thoughtful note. You’ve earned a customer for life.

comment:
First of all, please don’t misunderstand me—your Beef & Pickles sandwich is absolutely delicious. In fact, I came back for a second day in a row because it’s genuinely one of the best sandwiches I’ve ever had.

Unfortunately, my experience this morning completely ruined what had otherwise been a great impression.

Normally, I don’t pay much attention to prices. However, when I was charged $43 for two sandwiches, I was a little confused because the menu outside clearly listed them at $17.50 each. When I collected my order, I politely asked the young lady at the counter:

“Sorry, I’m just a little confused. The menu outside says the sandwich is $17.50, so could you please explain why I was charged $43 for two?”

In my opinion, asking a simple question like this is a customer’s most basic right.

However, the moment I asked, the young woman in the red shirt who was making coffee looked at me with an expression that made me extremely uncomfortable. It was a look of annoyance, impatience, and complete disdain—as if my question was somehow ridiculous. She rolled her eyes and looked at me with obvious contempt.

At that moment, I honestly wanted to ask her three questions:

1. I wasn’t even speaking to you.
2. As a paying customer, do I not have the right to ask a simple question?
3. As someone working in hospitality, have you completely forgotten the basic standards of professionalism and respect?

There were several other customers waiting to collect their orders at the time. Although I was upset and wanted to confront her, I didn’t want to hold everyone else up. The staff member at the counter answered my question professionally, so I simply thanked her and left.

But after I got home, I couldn’t stop thinking about what had happened. The whole interaction left me feeling genuinely uncomfortable.

That’s why I’ve decided to share this experience publicly here, and I will also be forwarding this feedback, exactly as written, to your head office management.

Your food is excellent, and that’s exactly why this experience was so disappointing.

When you’re charging more than $20 for a sandwich, customers expect more than just great food—they also expect the most basic level of courtesy and respect.

I sincerely hope the company continues maintaining its food quality while also placing greater emphasis on staff training, professionalism, and customer service. Respect costs nothing, but it means everything.

I’ve always had great experiences at Hector’s Deli in South Melbourne — even when they’re slammed with lines out the door, the staff are friendly, understanding, and happy to accommodate requests. Sadly, my first visit to the Fitzroy location was the complete opposite.

As we were about to walk in (through the wide-open door), a staff member (with tattoos on her arms) yelled at us to order from the side instead. I now understand that inside is for pick-up and outside is for ordering, but at the time we didn’t know. Even if we had stepped inside, it really wasn’t a big deal — she could’ve politely said, “Do you mind ordering from the side?” Instead, she shouted at us in a rude, unnecessarily loud tone that immediately set the wrong mood.

We then asked for a simple modification to avoid pork contamination — such as using baking paper or the wrapper to toast the sandwich, or even wiping down the toaster. Each time, she cut us off with a loud, condescending “NOOOO SORRY.” The chef, Chin, was the complete opposite: polite, friendly, and clearly willing to help. But she wouldn’t even let him get a word in.

Because of this, we ended up with cold tuna melt and cold meat sandwiches. Being from out of town, we didn’t have enough time to find other options, which made the experience even more disappointing.

It’s a shame that one staff member’s attitude can drag down the whole experience for the team. I won’t be returning to the Fitzroy store, especially knowing how much better and more accommodating the South Melbourne team is.

Edit: I emailed hectors deli, twice, as per their reply to my review, no response.

comment:
One of Melbourne’s food “icons,” so I couldn’t skip it. I chose the South Melbourne branch since it’s closer to home and feels more spacious than the CBD location. I went around lunchtime and the place was packed, with a long queue outside. We waited about 10 minutes to order, and the Maple Donut was already sold out, even though it was only midday.

We ordered 2 items:
- Beef and Pickles Toast (add Hectic sauce and cheese): a must-try signature. The smoked beef was thinly sliced and tender, the pickles were lightly tangy without being too salty, and the Hectic sauce with cheese added a rich, satisfying layer. It balanced out the crispy bread, which leaned slightly dry on its own.
- Chicken Salad Sandwich: I was choosing between this and the fried chicken, and picked the salad version to keep things lighter. It didn’t quite work for me. The filling was fresh, slightly tangy, and on the healthier side, but the cold savoury combination didn’t appeal to my taste, and the shredded chicken felt a bit plain.

I’d come back, but probably not anytime soon. It’s good, but not something I’d keep craving.

comment:

My sandwich had a layer of rocket leaves, their sauce which was quite sour and tangy, salamis and the chilli relish. Flavour was ok, would have made it slightly differently myself, but ok regardless.
The day before, another colleague had half of her salad sandwich left which I had. It was also just average, the extreme tangy and sour tone did not make it taste balanced at all. Vegetables were cruchy, especially the beetroot.
Will i go back and try again? Very reluctant, only if there is no line out the door. And I will likely try their mushroom melt as my colleague said that hers was quite good.

comment:
Hector’s Deli in South Melbourne is one of my favourite sandwich spots and the place where I first discovered the brand a few years ago. Their coffee is excellent, but the real star of the show here is definitely the sandwiches.

My go to order is the beef and pickles and I always add their signature “hectic” sauce. It is seriously elite. The sandwiches are packed with fresh ingredients and always incredibly satisfying.

I also really like their breakfast muffins. They remind me of a much fancier version of a McDonald’s sausage and egg McMuffin, and of course I add the hectic sauce to that as well.

This was also the location where I first tried their original maple glazed donuts, which are so good.

Over the years I have also tried the mushroom melt, tuna melt and the side salad, but the beef and pickles is still my favourite.

Service is always super friendly and efficient. There is a small amount of seating inside and some outdoor seating as well, but these days there is almost always a line of people waiting for takeaway which tells you how popular it has become.

I will be honest, these are not cheap sandwiches. If the idea of spending $15 to $20 on a sandwich makes you uncomfortable then this might not be the place for you. That said, I genuinely think they are worth every dollar and I would highly recommend trying it at least once.

I am also a bit of a sucker for their branding. It manages to feel both minimalist and slightly retro at the same time, and they really nail that balance.

Overall it is a consistently great spot for a seriously good sandwich.

comment:
I recently stopped by Hector's Deli and honestly… it might have ruined all other sandwiches for me.

First of all, the place has that perfect casual Melbourne vibe—busy, a bit chaotic, but in the fun “you know the food is going to be good” kind of way. The smell alone when you walk in should probably be bottled and sold as perfume.

The sandwich itself? Absolutely stacked. Fresh bread, super generous fillings, and everything perfectly balanced. You can tell they care about the ingredients, but they’re not being pretentious about it. It’s just a really, really good sandwich done right.

Service was quick even though it was packed, and the staff were friendly and efficient. You grab your food, find a spot outside, and suddenly life feels pretty good.

My only complaint: I spent the rest of the day thinking about that sandwich and wondering if it would be socially acceptable to go back for another one immediately. (For research purposes, of course.)

If you’re in South Melbourne and like sandwiches—even a little—this place is 100% worth the stop. Just be warned: you may start comparing every future sandwich to Hector’s… and most of them will lose. 🥪

comment: Came here in the early morning and ordered the pork shoulder sandwich, glazed donut and a flat white. Started off with the glazed donut and it was soft and pillowy with just the right amount of sweetness which paired well with the coffee. Then I had the pork shoulder sandwich which had pickled fennel, Calabrian chilli paste and kale pesto. The bread had a pleasant chew to it and a nice crust covered in toasted sesame seeds. Pork shoulder was thinly sliced so the meat was very tender and the sandwich was packed with flavour from the creamy kale pesto, refreshing pickled fennel and a gentle heat from the chilli paste. It was fresh and tasty but could be a little bit more generous with the amount of meat. Also tried the fried chicken a few days later which is available from 11am and you can choose between thigh or breast piece. I went with the breast piece and it was very tender and also quite big. It is served with a herby tarragon butter, crisp iceberg lettuce and tangy pickle mayo on a steamed milk bun which was very soft and spongy; very tasty.

comment:
I was surprised to see a Hector’s Deli kiosk pop up on Bourke Street right outside the H&M store this week. I absolutely love their other locations in Little Collins, South Melbourne and the bigger one in Richmond with all the pastries, so I had to stop when I spotted it.

Even though it was only 10am I could not resist grabbing a maple glazed donut and it did not disappoint. So good.

This kiosk seems to focus just on pastries rather than the sandwiches they are known for, which makes it more of a quick grab and go stop. The pastries looked great and everything felt very on brand for Hector’s.

My only suggestion would be to offer some kind of coffee option as well. Even something simple like canned iced lattes would be perfect because I definitely would have grabbed one with the donut.

Still a great little addition to the CBD and a dangerous discovery for anyone who already loves Hector’s like I do.
